WRITTEN ANSWERS TO STARRED QUESTIONS 
 Electrification of villages in Uttar Pradesh 
*421. SHRI BHAGWATI SINGH: Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to 
state: 
(a) the details of villages in Uttar Pradesh where electrification is yet to be 
done; 
(b) the details of Government's rural electrification scheme: and 
(c) by when electrification work in all the villages in Uttar Pradesh will be 
done by Government? 
 
1 
 

RAJYA SABHA [25 August, 2004] 
THE MINISTER OF POWER (SHRI P. M. SAYEED): (a) In Uttar 
Pradesh, there are 40080 villages yet to be electrified as on 31.03.04. 
(b) To achieve the objective of the National Common Minimum Programme 
of completing rural household electrification in five years a new strategy 
has been drawn up, which envisages: 
(i) Creation of Rural Electricity Distribution Backbone (REDB) of 33/11 KV 
substations, with at least one such substation in each block appropriately 
networked and linked to the State transmission system. 
(ii) Creation of Village Electricity  Infrastructure (VEI) by providing 
Distribution Transformers) with at l east one such transformer in every 
village. 
(iii) Rural Households Electification of unetectrified households from village 
distribution transformer(s). 
(iv) Decentralized distributed generation system for such villages where grid 
connectivity is either not feasible or not cost effective. 
(c) Uttar Pradesh has been advised to target completion of village elec 
trification by the end of the 10th Plan. 
1000 MV power plant in Maharashtra 
*422. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA: Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that NTPC had decided to set up a 1000 MW power 
plant at Mauda in Nagpur district of Maharashtra and so far about Rs. one crore 
has already been spent; 
(b) the present status of this power project and by when it is likely to be 
completed; and 
(c) the total deficit of power in Vidarbha and Marathwada regions of 
Maharashtra and what steps are proposed to be taken to meet the total demand? 
THE MINISTER OF POWER (SHRI P. M. SAYEED): (a) and (b) NTPC has 
identified a site for development of a 1000 MW power plant at Mauda in Nagpur 
District of Maharashtra. Works for various site specific studies 
 
2 

[25 August, 2004] RAJYA SABHA 
such as Topographical Survey, Geo-Tech nical Investigation, Seismic Study, 
Environmental Impact Assessment Study and Make-Up; Water Study etc., for the 
project have been taken up by NTPC to examine the Techno-Eco-nomic viability 
of the project. So far, approximately Rs.21 lakhs have been spent on various 
site specific studies mentioned above. 
Government of Maharashtra (GOM) conveyed its in-principle clearance for 
availability of 50 Million Cubic Metres of Water for the project from 
Gosikhurd Irrigation Project and which is expected to be completed within three 
years, once their fund requirement is tied-up. The confirmation of funding tie-
up and time frame for assured water supply is still awaited from Maharashtra 
Government. 
Coal availability from the near by coal mines is required to be confirmed. 
Setting up of the project will be taken up depending upon the establishment of 
Techno-Economic viability of the project. 
(c) As reported by Maharashtra Stat e Electricity Board (MSEB), re-gion-
wise power demand and supply study is not carried out. The study is carried out 
for the entire MSEB system. Central Electricity Authority (CEA) have informed 
that the total peak and energy deficit of power in the State of Maharashtra during the 
period April-July, 2004 and 3,102 MW (21.3%) and 2818 Million Units (9.5%) 
respectively. 
To meet the power deficits, Maharashtra has proposed a capacity addition of 
1950 MW is in 10 th Plan in the State sector. Maha rashtra is also entitled to a 
share of 1074 MW during Tenth Plan from central projects.

New strategy to tackle Naxalite menace 
*425. SHRI S.P.M. SYED KHAN: Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government are evolving a new strategy following the recent 
meet of State Chief Secretaries and DGs to tackle the growing menace of

4

(b) if so, the steps proposed to be taken by the Centre;

modernization and strengthening of  State Police Forces, long term

Problems of powerloom owners in Maharashtra 
*427. SHRI SANJAY RAJARAM RAUT: Will the Minister of 
TEXTILES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government are aware that powerloom owners in 
Maharashtra are facing problems and seeking Central Government's help; 
and 
(b) if so, the details of effective steps taken for the benefit of powerloom 
sector in Maharashtra? 
THE MINISTER OF TEXTILES (SHRI SHANKERSINH VAGHELA): 
(a) and (b) The Government had be en receiving requests from the 
Maharashtra powerloom industry for removal of CENVAT. In this year's 
budget the following important announcements have been made for the 
textile sector as a whole including the powerloom sector:— 
• Except for mandatory excise duty on polyester filament yarn including 
texturised yarn, synthetic and artificial fibres and synthetic and 
artificial filament yarns, the whole value addition chain has been given 
excise exemption option. 
• This excise exemption has been given across the value addition chain. 
For those, opting to pay duty and avail CENVAT credit, two rates of 
duty have been given as under: - 
• All textile goods made of pure cotton, not containing any other textile 
material—4% 
• Other textile goods—8% 
• Additional Excise Duty on Textiles and Textile Articles (AT&T) and 
Additional Excise Duty (Goods of Special Importance) Act have been 
abolished. 
Following steps have been taken for modernisation of the powerloom 
sector:- 
• Incentives have been made available under the Technology 
Upgradation Fund Scheme (TUFS) whereby the powerloom owner 
can reduce the cost of borrowing capital either by availing 20% upfront 
Capital Linked Subsidy or by obtaining 5% interest reimbursement 
of on the loan availed. 
7 

RAJYA  SABHA [25 August, 2004] 
* Government has announced a Scheme for assistance for construction of Group 
Workshed for powerlooms to create a better working environment and 
obtain high productivity. 
* Import of shuttleless looms has been allowed under concessional 
customs duty of 5% without countervailing duty. Excise exemption has 
also been given on such looms. 
* Accelerated depreciation benefits at the rate of 50% have been extended 
on the weaving machinery installed under TUFS. 
* Government has taken up modernization and strengthening of 
Powerloom Service Centres (PSCs), which have been set up to provide 
technical services of training, testing, project preparation etc. 
* Computer Aided Design Centres have been set up to enable small 
powerloom units to access new designs and upgrade fabric by product 
development inputs.

Human lives lost 1698 
Houses damaged 15,76,992

(c) The State Governments are primarily responsible for relief and rehabilitation

pleased to state: 
(a) whether there is any scheme to upgrade handloom and handicraft 
industry and technology; 
(b) if so, the details thereof including the action taken thereon and funds

THE MINISTER OF TEXTILES (SHRI SHANKERSINH VAGHELA): (a) to 
(b) Yes, Sir. The Government have been implementing following schemes to upgrade 
handloom, handicraft industry and technology: 
(i) Deen Dayal Hathkargha Protsahan Yojana (DDHPY): The scheme 
envisages assistance for product deve lopment, infrastructural support, 
institutional support, supply of equipments, and marketing support etc. 
both at macro and micro levels in an integrated and coordinated manner for 
an overall development of the handloom sector. 
(ii) Handloom Export Scheme: The scheme provides for-financial 
assistance to handloom agencies  for building, developing and 
marketing of exportable products. 
(iii) Integrated Handloom Training Project (IHTP): The scheme was 
introduced in December 2003 and it provides assistance for skill 
upgradation in weaving, dyeing, design development and managerial skills. 
(iv) Baba Saheb AmbedkarHastshilp Vikas Yojana: The main objective of this 
Scheme is to organize artisans' clusters into Self Help Groups

is to provide adequate support to National level institutes like IICT, 
MHSC, NCDCD etc. for upgradation of artisans skills through appropriate 
design and technical intervention to enable them to produce innovative 
and value-added items to cope with the fast changing market demand. 
The Statement showing funds allotted/released State-wise for the last three 
years, year-wise and scheme-wise is given the enclosed Statement I and II (See

(c) Yes, Sir.

Mathania Solar Energy Plant in Rajasthan 
†*436. DR. NARAYAN SINGH MANAKLAO: Will the Minister of NON-
CONVENTIONAL ENERGY SOURCES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the installation and construction work of 
Mathania Solar Energy Plant in Jodhpur district of Rajasthan is pending for 
more than a decade; 
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and 
(c) by when it is likely to be started and completed? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF TH E MINISTRY OF NON-CONVEN-
TIONAL ENERGY SOURCES (SHRI VILAS MUTTEMWAR): (a) and (b) 
While the proposal for the establishment of a solar thermal power plant at 
.Mathania in the Jodhpur district of Rajasthan has been under development and 
consideration for a long-time, the final detailed project report acceptable to 
various funding agencies was submitted only in the year 1998. After techno-
economic evaluation and appraisal, the project was sanc- 
† Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 
23 

RAJYA SABHA [25 August, 2004] 
tioned by the Government in the year 2000. The project envisaged the establishment of 
a 140 MW Integrated Solar Combined Cycle power plant with naphtha as the fuel for 
the combined cycle part. Due to a sharp increase in the prices of naphtha it was decided in 
2001 to use Re-gasified Liquid Natural Gas (R-LNG) as a fuel. The Rajasthan Renewable 
Energy Corporation (RREC), the project implementing agency, went through the 
process of pre-qualification of contractors and inviting bids for turn-key execution and 
operation and maintenance of the project. As no financial bids were received inspite of 
repeated extensions, the RREC and their consultants prepared a modified bidding process. 
The RREC negotiated with Gas Authority of India Limited for the supply of natural gas 
to the project. These factors have resulted in delay in starting construction work of 
the project. 
The Ministry has considered it essential to go in for a review of the techno-
economic viability of the project because of the following factors:— 
(i) there has been change in the fuel component of the project from naphtha to gas for 
which a 350 km. long gas pipeline will need to be laid by GAIL, 
(ii) there may be a need to revise the project cost on account of change in prices of 
imported equipment, 
(iii) there is a general lowering of domestic lending rates which may render 
foreign loans unattractive, 
(iv) the power purchase agreement with suitable guarantees from the State Government 
is yet to be signed with the distribution companies, 
(v) doubts have been cast on the project's technical viability because of the inability of 
the bidders to give performance guarantees for the integrated plant, and 
(vi) CEA is examining the calculations submitted by RREC with gas as the fuel. 
(c)    It is not feasible to indicate a completion date for the project at this stage.

(SHRI SRIPRAKASH JAISWAL): (A) and (b) Yes, Sir. The youth are being

against them under law.

training.

2278.   SHRI MOOLCHAND MEENA: 
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY.

(a) whether the Supreme Court in its judgement delivered on 6th April, 
2004 has come down heavily on terrorism and has called upon the 
Government to curb terrorism which increases lawlessness and violence in 
the country; 
(b) if so, what are the steps Government have taken to curb terrorist 
activities in the country, as suggested by Supreme Court; and 
(c) to what extent, Union and State Governments have taken steps to curb 
the terrorist activities in the country? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN TH E MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI SRIPRAKASH JAISWAL): (a) The Supreme Court of India in its 
judgement dated 6.4.2004 has inter-alia observed that terrorism is one of the 
manifestations of increased lawlessness and cult of violence. 
(b) and (c) The Government has consistently pursued a strategy to counter 
terrorism which gives primacy to dialogue, democratic political processes 
and the rule of law. The Central Government in conjunction with the State 
Governments has adopted an integrated approach to contain terrorism. This 
approach includes, inter-alia, strengthening border management to check 
infiltration, pro-active action against the terrorists within the affected States, 
gearing up of intelligence machinery, improved technology, weaponry and 
equipment for security forces, both at the Centre and in the States, action as 
per law against overground support for the terrorists and bilateral and 
multilateral cooperation to combat global terrorism. Within this broad 
strategy and approach, the measures, tactics and dynamic deployment of 
security forces to counter the terrorist s are constantly reviewed, refined and 
monitored both at the Central level and in the States.

2279. PROF. SAIF-UD-DIN SOZ: Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS

reported that Delhi has become a major destination for trafficking of women and 
children; 
(b) whether Government are also aware that the NGO (Shakti Vahini) had 
put Delhi high in the list of globalized centres of flesh trade; and 
(c) if so, what remedial measures Government of India intend to take? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI S. REGUPATHY): (a) to (c) Yes, Sir. The Government is aware of the 
problem of trafficking of women and children in Delhi and has taken a number 
of steps to check this menace. The Indian Missions in countries from where 
call-girls are reportedly coming to India grant visas to young women only after 
a personal interview in which their family background and their interest in 
tourist places in India are ascertained. Production of return ticket showing date 
of return is insisted upon in such cases and frequency of their visits is 
monitored. Besides, Delhi Police keeps a watch on hotels, guest houses and 
other probable places from where operators of flesh trade are suspected to be 
working as also on the persons previsously involved or suspected to be involved in 
such activities; and conducts raids, inter-alia, on hotels, guest houses, farm 
houses, massage parlours, parks and other public places.

Special status to Rajasthan for reform in Power Sector 
†2308. DR. PRABHA THAKUR: Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Government and other institutions have 
appreciated the various steps taken by the Government of Rajasthan for  
 
† Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 
93 

RAJYA SABHA [25 August, 2004] 
reforms in power sector in spite of scarcity of water resources; 
(b) whether Government is formulating any plan to grant the status of special 
State to Rajasthan in view of the said fact; 
(c) if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF POWER (SHRI P.M. SAYEED): (a) to (d) The 
Government of India has started a scheme in 2000-01 called Accelerated Power 
Development Programme (APDP) to provide systematic finance to enable State 
Electricity Boards (SEBs)/ Utilities to ta ke distribution sector reform. The 
scheme has been rechristened as Accelerated Power Development & Reforms 
Programme (APDRP) in the year 2002-03. APDRP has two components. Under 
incentive component, assistance is provided as full grant to a State equivalent to 
50% of the reduction in operating cash tosses of power utility(ies). Agrant of Rs. 
137.71 crores has been released to Rajasthan as incentive during 2003-04 under 
APDRP. 
Under investment component of the APDRP, which is for assisting States in 
improving distribution network, special consideration has been accorded to Special 
Category States namely all the North Eastern States, Sikkim, Uttaranchal, 
Himachal Pradesh and Jammu & Kashmir. These States get APDRP assistance 
in the form of 90% grant and 10% loan. Remaining States get the assistance in 
the ratio of grant and loan on 1:1 basis. Rajasthan is covered under Non-Special 
Category States. 
The Special Category States covered under APDRP are those States which 
have been recognized as Special Category States by the National Development 
Council.

THE MINISTER OF POWER (SHRI P.M. SAYEED): (a) to (c) A revised 
draft National Electricity Policy has now been formulated based on comments 
received on the previous draft and th e objectives of the National Common 
Minimum Progamme. The views received fr om Stakeholders have also been 
taken into account. 
Draft National Electricity Policy now formulated aims at achieving the 
objectives of providing access to electri city to all households in next five 
years, fully meeting the demand of electricity, making available supply of 
reliable and quality power at reasonable rates and increasing per capita 
consumption to over 1000 units by year 2012. It addresses the issues of rural 
electrification, generation, transmission, distribution, technology de-
velopment, financing, private sector participation, energy conservation, 
promotion to renewable and non-conventional sources of energy, protection 
of consumers' interests etc. 
Draft National Electricity Policy envisages stepping up public sector 
investments, both at the Central Government and State Governments. A 
sizeable investment from private sector  is also envisaged considering the

Curtailment in Hydro-electric Power due to inadequate rainfall 
2317. SHRI EKANATH K. THAKUR: Will the Minister of POWER be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether the inadequate rainfall in the country has curtailed the hydro-
electricity generation in the country; and 
(b) if so, the measures Government propose to take to meet contingencies like 
this and augment power generation? 
THE MINISTER OF POWER (SHRI P.M. SAYEED): (a) Generation 
from hydro power stations is dependent upon the pattern of rainfall in the 
catchment areas and reservoir level/inflows in the reservoirs of reservoir based 
hydro power stations. This year, due to inadequate rainfall, generation from hydro 
power stations has been affected. As against (generation target of 33,737 MUs 
for the period 1st April, 2004 to 17th August, 2004, hydel generation has been 
33,001 MUs representing a shortfall of 736 MUs ( i.e. 2.2%). The shortfall in 
hydel generation during the period 1s t April to 17th A ugust, 2004 accounts 
for meager 0.33% of the overall generation target during this period. 
(b) The following steps are being taken to boost the generation to make up the 
loss in hydel generation: 
(i) Postponement of planned maintenance of thermal generating units. 
(ii) Bringing back the thermal generating units already taken under planned 
shutdown on war footing. 
(iii) Increase in generation from existing thermal units. 
(iv) Close monitoring for ensuring supply of adequate coal to the power plants. 
(v) Maximization of generation from gas/liquid fuel plants. 
(vi) Ensuring maximum transfer of power from surplus regions/States to deficit 
regions/States.

Drinking water programmes 
†2346. SHRI PYARELAL KHANDELWAL: Will the Mjnister of RURAL 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of the programmes formulated by Government for providing safe 
potable water; 
(b) what is 'Sampurna Swachchhta Abhiyan' and how does it reach the 
villages; and 
(c) the number of NGOs involved in the said programme in M.P. and the details 
thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRI A. NARENDRA): (a) Water supply is a State 
subject. State Governments are primarily responsible for provinding drinking water 
facilities to rural habitations. Government of India supplement the efforts of 
the States in providing drinking water facilities to the rural habitations 
through a Centrally Spon sored Scheme namely "A ccelerated Rural Water 
Supply Programme (ARWSP)." Annual allocations made under ARWSP are 
utilized for different purposes, namely, rural water supply schemes, community 
based rural water supply schemes like Swajaldhara and Sector Reform Projects, 
water quality mitigation schemes, sustainability related projects and calamity 
relief etc. 
(b) 'Sampurna Swachchhta Abhiyan' or Total Sanitation Campaign (TSC)' is a 
programme launched to improve the ru ral sanitation coverage with active 
participation of the community. It is a demand driven programme for generating 
demand for basic sanitation facilities in household, schools, community and 
public places by creating awareness of and bringing attitudinal changes for 
relevant sanitation and hygiene practices. TSC is sanctioned taking district as a 
unit and Central funds are released to the district implementing agency which 
could be Zilla Parishad, District Rural Development Agency or District Water 
and Sanitation Mission, who in turn releases funds to villages. 
(c) NGOs play a significant role for taking up information, education, 
communication, capacity development activities and social mobilization at 
district and village levels. The engagement of NGOs is done by district 
implementing agencies only. Details of NGOs engaged by district

implementing agencies in different States are not kept at Government of India 
level.

under Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana; 
(b) whether these wages are uniform in all the States of the 
country; 
(c) if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRIMATI SURYAKANTA PATIL): (a) to (d) Rural roads is 
a State subject and funds under the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) 
are released to State Government agencies for construction of rural roads. 
Contracts for construction are entered into by State Government agencies. The 
Standard Bidding Document prescribed under the PMGSY provides that the 
contractor is to pay not less than the minimum wages as per the provisions of 
Minimum Wages Act, 1948. The Act empowers the State Governments to fix 
the minimum wages. There is no requirement that the wages sould be uniform 
in all the States.

sanitation besides the earlier parameters, i.e. level of calories consumption; and

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRIMATI SURYAKANTA PATIL): (a) and (b) The official

Quinquennial Consumer Expenditure Survey conducted by the National Sample 
Survey Organization (NSSO). The official poverty line is anchored on the per 
capita monthly expenditure corresponding to per capita daily calorie 
requirement of 2400 in rural areas and 2100 in urban areas. The poverty line 
defined in this way covers not only the expenditure on food but also on non-food 
items such as clothing, housing, health and education and social services. The 
Government are not contemplating to redefine the poverty line so far as the 
Ministry of Rural Development is concerned.

"Swarnjayanti Swarozgar Yojana' for increasing the agricultural

productivity through optimum utilization of locally available resources and

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRI MATISURYAKANTA PATIL): (a) and (b) Ascheme 
captioned Swarnjayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY) is being 
implemented by the Government with effect from 1.4.1999. The objective of 
SGSY is to bring the assisted poor families (Swarozgaris) above the poverty 
line by ensuring appreciable increase in incomes over a period of time. This 
objective is to be achieved inter-alia by organizing, the rural poor into Self 
Help Groups (SHGs) through a process of social mobilization, their training and 
capacity building and provision of income-generating assets through a mix of 
bank credit and Government subsidy. The selection of activities under the scheme is 
based on the local resources, the aptitude and skill of the intended Swarozgaris 
and market potential for products. The scheme focuses on vulnerable section of 
the society including women and socially challenged sections. As per guidelines 
of the scheme, 50% of the group formed in each block should be exclusively 
for the women. Further, women, SCs/STs and disabled are to account for at 
least 40%, 50% and 3% of the assisted swarozgaris respectively. The amount 
released by Government of India since inception of the scheme, year-wise and 
State-wise is given in the enclosed Statement (See below).

2360. SHRI EKANATH K. THAKUR: Will the Minister of TEXTILES be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that handicrafts and handloom weaving industry in the 
country has been dropped out of the mainstream development agenda; 
(b) whether Government are aware of the fact that millions of artisans in India 
are forced to remain in the backwaters of market economy as the craft clusters 
of India are still outside the mainstream marketing infrastructure; and 
(c) if so, the steps Government propose to take to improve the market access 
of crafts in the country? 
THE MINISTER OF TEXTILES (SHRI SHANKERSINH VAGHELA): (a) 
No, Sir. 
(b) and (c) No, Sir. Market Support Serv ices is implemented as one of the 
priority areas for promotion and development of the handicraft sector. Under the 
Marketing Support Services Scheme and Baba Saheb Ambedkar Hastshilp Vikas 
Yojana (AHVY), assistance is made available to organize marketing events viz. 
National Handicrafts Expos, Crafts Bazaars and Exhibitions, Fairs and 
Festivals at strategic locations throughout the country, in which the artisans 
are invited to sell their products directly. Assistance is also provided for 
creating marketing infrastructure such as setting up of Urban Haats, Emporia etc. 
through various agencies, to provide permanent marketing outlets to the artisans. 
Further emphasis is also being laid towards promotion of export of 
handicrafts clusters through increased participation in International fairs/ 
exhibitions abroad, tapping new unexplored markets, product diversification as per 
market demand, improved quality and packaging, aggressive publicity etc.

Recommendations of the National Commission on Youth 
†2369. SHRI MANGANI LAL MANDAL: Will th e Minister of YOUTH 
AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Government had set up a National Commission in 
March 2002, keeping in view the problem being faced by unemployed youth and 
the report of the Commission was scheduled to be received by Government in 
March, 2004; and 
(b) if so, the outcome thereof and the recommendation in the Report 
received by Government alongwith the action taken in this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRSAND SPORTS (SHRI SUNIL DUTT): (a) 
and (b) Yes, Sir. A National Commi ssion for Youth was set up by the 
Government in March 2002. The Commission submitted the Executive 
Summary of the Report to the Government on 7th February, 2004 and was to 
submit its Report by March, 2004. As the Commission required more time for 
detailed examination of the many reports of the research studies the result of 
which may have a significant bearing on its Report, its tenure was extended 
beyond 31st March, 2004. The Commission finally submitted its Report to the 
Government on 16th July, 2004. The major recommendations of the Commission 
include creation of a Central Authority, merger of various youth related schemes, 
creation of a new Statutory Body at national level, establishment of an Inter-
Departmental Committee on Youth Affairs, setting up of a National Bank for 
Youth, making Skill and Vocational training a part of the curricula in schools from 
middle level and recommendations for youth of North Eastern Region. The 
Report and recommendations of the Commission are being examined by the 
Government.

† 2371. SHRI MANGANI LAL MANDAL: Will the Minister of YOUTH 
AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Government after adopting the National Youth 
Policy, 2003, have started implementing the same in order to make youth of the 
country actively participate in National Development as also to inspire them; 
and 
(b) if so, the primary areas, activities and priorities of the policy alongwith the 
mode of its implementation in Bihar including other States and the amount 
spent on this so far alongwith the results thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS (SHRI SUNIL 
DUTT): (a) and (b) Yes, Sir. Government have adopted the National Youth Policy, 
2003 for all-round development of the youth. The Policy has also streesed the 
need to involve the youth in various programmes and activities for National 
development. 
The Policy has recognised four thrust areas i.e. Youth Empowerment; Gender 
Justice; Inter-Sectoral Approach; and Information and Research Network; 
It has identified the following areas as Key Sectors of concern for the 
youth:— 
(a) Education; (b) Training and Employment; (c) Health and Family 
Welfare; (d) Preservation of Environment, Ecology and Wild life; (e)

†2378. SHRI NARAYAN SINGH KESRI: Will the Minister of YOUTH 
AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of the programmes being run by Government to promote sports 
amongst young men/women and students of Scheduled Castes and weaker 
sections; 
(b) whether any programme is being operated by Government to bring the 
young men/women of Scheduled Caste Community in the mainstream; 
(c) if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) the role of 'Nehru Youth Centre' in this direction? 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS (SHRI SUNIL 
DUTT): (a) to (c) All the sports promotion programmes of the Ministry are 
implemented through general schemes. There is no such scheme specifically 
meant for Scheduled Castes and weaker sections. However, Sports Authority of 
India (SAI) through its schemes like National Sports Talent contest Scheme 
(NSTC) and Special Area Games Centre (SAG) cater specifically to induct 
talent from the remote, backward, tribal, coastal, hilly regions of the country 
and provide them sports training along with other sections of the community. 
(d) Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan (NYKS) is implementing two types of 
programmes through its district level kendras, which are promoting sports 
amongst all sections of youth including scheduled castes and weaker sections. The 
details of the above two programmes are as under: 
Sports Promotion Programmes 
The main objective of the Programme is to promote sports culture and 
sportsmanship among rural youth and to improve sports scenario in rural areas. It 
also aims at popularizing rural sports and games which require minimum 
infrastructure, equipment and finance. Each NYK has to organize three Sports 
Promotion Programmes and a sum of Rs.5000/- is allotted to each programme.

Rural Sports Clubs 
The principal objective of this scheme is to help the emergence of a countrywide 
network of Sports Club Culture for channelizing the energies of youth for constructive 
activities on one hand and exploring and nurturing sports talent in rural and tribal areas on 
the others. Funds to the tune of Rs.30,000/- (normal area) and Rs.45,000/- (tribal area) are 
earmarked for each such club. NYKS has been entrusted with the responsibility to 
implement this scheme.
